records.text: Paper card. Question: Can sol-gel autocombustion be used to synthesize nanocrystalline high-entropy alloys?. System: CoCrCuNiAl high-entropy alloy. Processing: Sol-gel autocombustion with fuel-oxidant ratio of 1:1. Test conditions: Room temperature, argon atmosphere. Findings: Average grain size of 14 nm; Excellent uniform dispersion; Distinctive magnetic behavior similar to superparamagnetic behavior; Saturated magnetizations of 13.372 emu/g; Lower remanence ratio of 1.93%; Lower coercivity force of 10.528 Oe. Mechanism: Chelation between citric acid and metal ions, in situ chemical reactions. Quote: "a novel sol–gel autocombustion technique was first used to synthesize high-entropy alloys"
